# TR4W radio-factory capabilities vs HamLib rig backends -- offline cross-check

**Generated by** `tools/hamlib-crosscheck/crosscheck.py` (rerunnable, no args).
**HamLib reference:** `C:\Users\toms\projects\Hamlib`, commit `c7fb0fa` (2026-07-25 12:36:52 -0500) -- `rigs/` backend sources ONLY;
the `simulators/` directory is deliberately ignored (the project has established
that the sims contradict the library).

## Purpose and methodology

This is a build-time text-parse comparison of what each TR4W factory radio
declares in `FCapabilities.Flags` / `CWSpeedMin..Max` / `SerialParams(...)`
against what the corresponding HamLib `struct rig_caps` states. The join key is
the `hamlibID` column of `RadioParametersArray` in `tr4w/src/trdos/LOGRADIO.PAS`.

**Evidence asymmetry (core rule):** an independent implementation is EVIDENCE
when it STATES something and close to WORTHLESS when it OMITS something.
A disagreement where HamLib states a capability that TR4W denies is a STRONG
lead; where HamLib merely lacks something TR4W claims, it is a WEAK lead.

**This report proposes BENCH LEADS, never automatic changes.** Nothing here is
evidence enough on its own to flip a capability flag; each lead needs a bench
check on the real rig (or a manual citation) first.

**Known caveat for Section A (stated up front):** for several non-Icom families
the factory declares only the flags something currently consumes. The project's
own comment (uRadioYaesuASCIILegacy.pas:148-158) says absence can mean "TR4W
does not poll it", not "the radio cannot". Rows below carry a note when the
TR4W driver visibly reads the state anyway; those are documentation gaps rather
than functional leads.

Flag-to-caps mapping used: rcReadVFOB <- `.targetable_vfo` has RIG_TARGETABLE_FREQ;
rcReadRIT <- `.get_rit`; rcReadSplit <- `.get_split_vfo`; rcReadTXStatus <- `.get_ptt`;
rcCWByCAT <- `.send_morse`; rcCWSpeedSync <- RIG_LEVEL_KEYSPD in `.has_get/set_level`;
rcPlayDVK <- `.send_voice_mem` (approximate -- HamLib's voice-memory API is newer and
thinly implemented, so its absence is especially weak evidence). rcDataMode,
rcSharedRITXITOffset and rcCWFlushDisruptsTiming have no per-model HamLib analogue
and are not cross-checked (rcCWFlushDisruptsTiming is a TR4W send-queue mechanism;
every CI-V radio carries it by design).

|---|---|
| TR4W factory registrations (enum-keyed) | 92 |
| ... with a hamlibID in RadioParametersArray | 89 |
| ... joined to a parsed HamLib caps struct | 87 |
| HamLib caps structs parsed (all rigs/) | 321 |
| Flag comparisons in agreement | 411 |

## Section C -- serial-parameter disagreements

TR4W registration `SerialParams(baud, data, parity, stop)` vs hamlib
`serial_rate_min/max`, `serial_data_bits`, `serial_stop_bits`, `serial_parity`.
A TR4W default baud inside hamlib's range is NOT a finding (defaults may differ).

**Known deliberate divergence:** OMNI6 uses **1 stop bit** per its Model 563
manual section 5.2 (bench-decided). If hamlib disagrees below, hamlib is the one
likely wrong -- do not flag TR4W.

**Caution on stop bits generally:** hamlib caps state what hamlib SENDS, not what
the rig requires (a UART receiving with 1 stop bit accepts 2-stop-bit frames).
Classic Kenwood serial protocol docs specify 4800 baud with 2 stop bits, so for
the older Kenwoods TR4W's 2 is likely the manual-correct value and hamlib's 1 the
permissive one. The Elecraft rows (default 8N1 per Elecraft's programmer's
reference) are the ones most worth a bench/manual check.

## Section D -- CW keyer speed range disagreements

Only radios where TR4W declares a non-zero range AND hamlib's level_gran gives a
KEYSPD range. Note hamlib backends mostly inherit a family-wide default from
`level_gran_<backend>.h` (e.g. 4..60), so a mismatch here is usually hamlib being
generic rather than TR4W being wrong -- weigh these as weak-to-medium leads and
check the rig manual, not hamlib, for the truth.

## Section E -- suspect hamlibID values in RadioParametersArray

These enum rows carry a hamlibID that resolves to a DIFFERENT radio in this
HamLib checkout. They are excluded from Sections A-D (the join would compare
the wrong rig), and they are findings in their own right: the hamlibID is what
TR4W hands to HamLib when a radio is driven through the HamLib path, so a wrong
ID there drives the rig with another model's backend. Verify against the
riglist of the HamLib version TR4W actually ships (`libhamlib-4.dll`) before
changing anything -- IDs are stable in HamLib, but the shipped list is the
authority.

| TR4W enum | hamlibID in LOGRADIO | resolves to | name-matching candidates in riglist.h |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLEX (FlexRadio 6000) | 2048 | POWERSDR (rigs/kenwood/flex6xxx.c:1478) | (none by name) |
| TS2000 (Kenwood TS-2000) | 2041 | TS890S (rigs/kenwood/ts890s.c:536) | TS2000 = 2014 |
| TS590 (Kenwood TS-590) | 2004 | TS570D (rigs/kenwood/ts570.c:1098) | TS590S = 2031, TS590SG = 2037 |

FLEX = 2048 is RIG_MODEL_POWERSDR (the PowerSDR/Flex-5000-era backend).
The factory registration is 'FlexRadio 6000'; HamLib's 6000-series model is
RIG_MODEL_F6K = 2036 (rigs/kenwood/flex6xxx.c). Possibly deliberate --
the ID predates the 6000 driver -- but worth a decision on record.

## Appendix -- unmappable / unresolved / limitations

### TR4W registrations with no hamlibID (unmappable)

- IC7300MK2 (Icom IC-7300MK2): no hamlibID in RadioParametersArray row
- IC905 (Icom IC-905): no hamlibID in RadioParametersArray row
- FT710 (Yaesu FT-710): no hamlibID in RadioParametersArray row

### TR4W registrations whose hamlibID has no parsed caps struct

- ORION (Ten-Tec Orion): hamlibID 16008 -> RIG_MODEL_TT565
- FTX1F (Yaesu FTX-1F): hamlibID 1051 -> RIG_MODEL_FTX1

### Enum members with NO factory registration (legacy/HamLib-only path)

These are in `InterfacedRadioType` but have no `RegisterRadio` call, so they are
not TR4W factory radios and are excluded from all sections above:

FT736R, FLRIG, TRXMANAGER, FT757GXII, EXPERTTCI, ACLOG, HAMLIBANY

### Special cases

- FLEX registers TWO driver classes (TFlexAPI + TFlexCAT); their capability sets were UNIONED
  for this comparison. HamLib's flex6xxx backend is a Kenwood-derived CAT
  driver, closest to TFlexCAT.
- TR4W maps its single TS570 entry to hamlibID 2016; hamlib splits TS-570D/TS-570S
  into two models with identical relevant caps.

### Parser limitations (honest list -- nothing silently truncated)

- Pascal side: capability statements are recognized only inside `Create`
  constructors and `DefineCapabilities` bodies (which is where the codebase puts
  them); a capability set anywhere else would be missed.
- `inherited Create` is assumed to run the nearest ancestor constructor (the
  intended semantics; the known bare-`inherited Create` overload trap would be a
  TR4W bug, not a parser feature).
- C side: no real preprocessor. Object-like #defines from the backend directory
  are expanded iteratively; #ifdef branches inside caps structs are all taken.
- HamLib "presence of a caps field" can be inherited generic code (e.g.
  `icom_mem_get_split_vfo`, `kenwood_get_rit`) that a given rig may NAK at run
  time -- exactly why every Section A row is a bench lead, not a fact.
